issue: Gain-contingency disclosure is described as optional: flashcard fc4 says "disclosure allowed if not misleading" and far-x3-30's item explanation says gain contingencies "may be disclosed". ASC 450-30-50-1 makes adequate disclosure mandatory ("shall"). The earlier remediation (REVIEW.md: far-cont-02, u12 t3, lesson changed "allowed" to "shall") missed these two places, so the platform now states the rule two ways.
evidence: ASC 450-30-50-1: "Adequate disclosure shall be made of a contingency that might result in a gain, but care shall be exercised to avoid misleading implications as to the likelihood of realization." The lesson says "Adequate disclosure shall be made", and far-cont-02 and u12 t3 say "is required". fc4 says "allowed". far-x3-30 says "may be disclosed", and its own choice (d) explanation says "Adequate disclosure is made". far-x3-30's key (c) is still correct.
source: FASB ASC 450-30-50-1; REVIEW.md remediation row for far-cont-02 / u12 t3 / lesson
fix: fc4 back: "Not recognized until **realized or realizable**; adequate disclosure **is required** (ASC 450-30-50-1), avoiding misleading implications about the likelihood of realization." far-x3-30 explanation: "ASC 450-30-25-1, 50-1: gain contingencies are not recognized before realization; adequate disclosure shall be made, taking care not to imply that realization is likely." Add both to the remediation pin test.

issue: Row t5 (Reyes guaranteed a $1,000,000 bank loan of an affiliate in Year 1; payment remote) is keyed "Disclose only", but what the platform teaches leads to "Recognize in Year 1 statements". The lesson, flashcard fc5 and far-cont-06 all say a guarantor recognizes a liability at inception for the fair value of the stand-ready obligation even if payment is not probable. "Disclose only" is right only under the ASC 460-10-25-1 scope exceptions (guarantees between a parent and its subsidiaries or between entities under common control). The exhibit never establishes that relationship, the lesson never teaches the exception, and the explanation ("Guarantees are disclosed even when the chance of loss is remote") addresses disclosure only, not why nothing is recognized.
evidence: Lesson: "Guarantees of others' debt: at inception, recognize a liability for the fair value of the stand-ready obligation (ASC 460), even if payment isn't probable." far-cont-06 keys "A liability of $30,000" when default is not probable. In u12 the guarantee was issued in Year 1, so a learner applying that rule picks "Recognize". Under ASC 460-10-25-1 [scope exceptions to recognition, incl. parent-subsidiary and common-control guarantees], recognition is exempt but disclosure (ASC 460-10-50-4) still applies. "Affiliate" is not tied to any relationship in the exhibit, and no fair value is given.
fix: Either (a) rewrite the exhibit: "Reyes guaranteed a $1,000,000 bank loan of Reyes Holdings' other subsidiary (an entity under common control with Reyes)…", and the explanation: "Guarantees between entities under common control are exempt from ASC 460's initial-recognition requirement (ASC 460-10-25-1) but not its disclosures; guarantees are disclosed even when loss is remote (ASC 460-10-50-4)"; add the exception to the lesson's guarantee paragraph. Or (b) make the borrower an unrelated supplier, give the guarantee's fair value, and key "Recognize in Year 1 statements".

issue: Pure-recall items are labeled skill "analysis" and difficulty 3, two skill levels too high. Each stem states the probability class and asks for the treatment, with no documents to interpret, no competing facts and no computation. Items testing the identical fact are labeled remembering/application at difficulty 1–2, so the labels are also inconsistent, and they inflate the module's apparent analysis share.
evidence: far-cont-19 "A loss is probable but can't be reasonably estimated. What is required?" (analysis, 3) duplicates far-cont-chk1 (application). far-cont-23 "reasonably possible… How is it reported?" (analysis, 3) duplicates far-cont-12 (application, 2) and pre1. far-cont-24 gain contingency (analysis, 3) duplicates far-cont-02 (application, 2) and far-x3-30 (remembering, 1). far-cont-28 unasserted claim (analysis, 3) duplicates far-cont-05 (application, 2). Blueprint: Remembering & Understanding = recall and understand; Analysis = examine and study interrelationships (FAR-III.B.3 "analyze supporting documentation such as legal letters").
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv FAR-III.B.1/B.3
fix: Set skill "remembering" and difficulty 1 for far-cont-19, -23, -24 and -28, or rewrite them as genuine analysis items (e.g., give an excerpt from a legal letter and ask for the treatment of several matters).

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are one level off and inconsistent across identical tasks. far-cont-20, -21, -22, -25 and -26 are one-step application items labeled analysis and difficulty 3. far-cont-11, -12 and -14 are rule recall labeled application.
evidence: far-cont-21/-22 (best estimate / minimum of a range: analysis, 3) duplicate far-cont-13/-16 (application, 2). far-cont-25 (1,000 × 5% × 200 − 3,000 = 7,000: analysis, 3) and far-cont-26 ((40,000 − 15,000) × 0.50 = 12,500: analysis, 3) mirror far-cont-03/-18 (application, 2). far-cont-20 (gross presentation: analysis, 3) is a single presentation rule. far-cont-11 and -12 have the same structure as far-cont-10 (remembering, 1). far-cont-14 asks for recall of the ASC 410-30-35-12 discounting rule (application, 3).
fix: far-cont-20, -21, -22, -25, -26 → application, difficulty 2. far-cont-11, -12, -14 → remembering (difficulty 1; keep 2 for -14 if it is seen as niche).

issue: The module has essentially no genuine analysis-level MCQs. Once the labels are corrected, the 31 practice and exam MCQs are about 35% remembering, 61% application and 3% analysis (only far-cont-27). The FAR targets are 5–15% R&U, 45–55% application and 35–45% analysis. Blueprint task FAR-III.B.3 (analyze legal letters and contracts to decide accrue, disclose or neither) is exercised only by the two TBS.
evidence: As labeled: application 17, analysis 10, remembering 4. After the relabels in the two findings above: remembering 11, application 19, analysis 1 (python count over items.json, practice and exam pools).
fix: Replace 4–5 of the redundant range and classification items with analysis MCQs. Examples: an attorney's-letter excerpt covering three matters, asking for total accrual and required disclosures; a schedule of matters with dates around the balance-sheet and issuance dates (contingency × subsequent events); a purchase-contract excerpt with a market decline and partial delivery.

issue: In all three "best estimate" items, the best estimate equals the midpoint of the range. A learner who wrongly applies the midpoint rule (the misconception the minimum-of-range items treat as the main trap) still gets them right, so they cannot tell the GAAP rule apart from the error. far-cont-13 distractor (d) $275,000 comes from no plausible error, and its explanation ("No averaging is used") does not say what it is.
evidence: far-cont-13: (200,000 + 500,000)/2 = 350,000 = keyed best estimate. far-cont-21: (100,000 + 300,000)/2 = 200,000 = key. far-x3-14: (100,000 + 400,000)/2 = 250,000 = key. 275,000 = (200,000 + 350,000)/2, which no candidate would compute. far-cont-07 does this correctly (best estimate 3.4M vs midpoint 3.5M).
fix: Move the best estimates off the midpoint and add a midpoint distractor. far-cont-13: best estimate $300,000, choices 300,000 / 200,000 / 500,000 / 350,000 (midpoint, wrong-rule). far-cont-21: best estimate $250,000, with $200,000 as the midpoint distractor. far-x3-14: best estimate $300,000, with $250,000 as the midpoint distractor.

issue: Range-of-loss accrual is tested the same way six times in the practice pool, plus twice in the exam pool, the lesson worked example, TBS r3 row A and TBS u12 row a1. That is well past the redundancy threshold (more than 3). far-cont-21 and far-cont-22 are consecutive and identical except for one clause, so each gives away the other: -21's key ($200,000) is -22's midpoint distractor.
evidence: Minimum of range: far-cont-01 (200–500k), far-cont-16 (100–400k), far-cont-22 (100–300k), far-x3-22 (200–500k). Best estimate: far-cont-07, far-cont-13, far-cont-21, far-x3-14. Stems differ only in the numbers. cues.md Jaccard: -13~-21 0.62, -16~-22 0.62, -21~-22 0.57.
fix: Retire far-cont-21 and far-cont-22, or convert them into multi-matter items (e.g., one probable range with a best estimate plus one reasonably possible claim, asking for the total accrual). Keep far-cont-01/-16 and far-cont-07/-13 as the single-concept items.

issue: Mock exam item far-x3-22 is a near-verbatim twin of practice item far-cont-01: same $200,000–$500,000 range, same "no amount more likely" fact, same key ($200,000) and the same distractor set ($350,000 midpoint, $500,000 maximum, $0). Mock items are meant to be unseen (REVIEW.md: the new exam-pool items "never appear in practice"), so this one rewards memory and inflates the mock score.
evidence: far-cont-01: "probable, with losses between $200,000 and $500,000 and no amount within the range more likely than another" → (d) $200,000. far-x3-22: "probable… between $200,000 and $500,000, with no amount in the range more likely than any other" → (c) $200,000.
fix: Rewrite far-x3-22 with different facts that need judgment, e.g., two matters (one probable with a range and no best estimate, one reasonably possible) asking for the total accrual, or at least change the range and context.

issue: The "calc" flag is set on items that need no computation. The answer is read straight from the stem (a range end point, a stated best estimate, a stated fair value or a stated loss), and items testing the identical task are flagged false.
evidence: far-cont-01/-22/far-x3-22 pick the minimum, far-cont-07/-13/-21 pick the stated best estimate, far-cont-06 picks the stated $30,000 fair value, far-cont-20 is a gross-vs-net presentation choice, and far-cont-27 picks the stated $80,000. far-cont-16 (same task as -22) has no calc flag, and far-x3-14 has calc:false. Schema: calc "set only for items that need a computation".
fix: Set calc:false on the nine items listed. Keep it on chk2, far-cont-03, -09, -18, -25 and -26.

issue: Trap labels and rationales that don't describe the error that produces the distractor.
evidence: far-cont-11(a) "Disclose only" is tagged partial-computation, but no computation is involved; the error is wrong-rule. far-cont-20(a) "$200,000 only" is tagged partial-computation, but it is netting the recovery against the liability, which is a wrong-rule/offsetting error. far-cont-22(a) is the $200,000 midpoint tagged wrong-classification, while the same midpoint error is tagged wrong-rule in far-cont-01, -16 and far-x3-22. far-cont-25(d): 13,000 = 10,000 + 3,000 (adds the repairs instead of subtracting them, a wrong-sign error), but it is tagged distractor-number with the rationale "Not the computation." far-cont-26(d): 42,500 = (100,000 − 15,000) × 0.50 (ignores the 40% expected-redemption rate, like far-cont-18(c)), but it is tagged distractor-number with "Not the computation." far-x3-30(a) recognizing the gain is tagged "reversed"; it is applying the loss-accrual rule to a gain (wrong-rule/overgeneralization).
fix: Set -11(a) wrong-rule; -20(a) wrong-rule ("Offsetting isn't permitted without a right of setoff (ASC 210-20-45-1)"); -22(a) wrong-rule; -25(d) wrong-sign ("Adds the $3,000 of repairs to the accrual instead of subtracting it"); -26(d) overgeneralization ("Assumes every outstanding coupon will be redeemed: 85,000 × $0.50; use the 40% expected rate"); x3-30(a) wrong-rule.

issue: Thin or circular explanations. Calculation items far-cont-18, -25 and -26 have item-level explanations with no numbers. Distractor rationales in -24, -25 and -26 are circular ("Not the treatment.", "Not the computation."). far-cont-04(b) "Gains follow different guidance." does not say why a gain contingency, which ASC 450-30-50-1 requires to be disclosed, is not the answer.
evidence: far-cont-18 item explanation: "The liability is the cost of expected remaining redemptions." far-cont-25: "…estimated total cost less costs already incurred." far-cont-26: "…expected redemptions not yet made times the cost per redemption." The schema comment requires "full computation when calculation-based". far-cont-24(b) and (c): "Not the treatment."
fix: -18: "100,000 × 40% = 40,000 expected; 40,000 − 10,000 redeemed = 30,000 × $2 = **60,000**." -25: "1,000 × 5% × $200 = 10,000 accrued − 3,000 spent = **7,000**." -26: "100,000 × 40% = 40,000; (40,000 − 15,000) × $0.50 = **12,500**." -24(b): "Deferred revenue requires cash received for goods or services still owed; nothing has been received." -24(c): "Recognizing the expected award as a reduction of expenses is still recognizing a gain contingency." -04(b): "A gain contingency has no loss; the remote-loss disclosure exception (ASC 450-20-50-6) is for guarantees."

issue: Lesson–item alignment: the practice items test several rules that this lesson, and no earlier FAR lesson, ever teaches. These are environmental-liability discounting (-14), self-insurance and uninsured risks (-15, also TBS r3 row F), probable insurance recoveries presented gross (-20), premium/coupon liabilities (-18, -26), the ban on general reserves, and "probable" vs more-likely-than-not (-08 a/b).
evidence: The lesson body has only the probability grid, ranges, assurance warranties, guarantees, gain contingencies and commitments. grep of content/far/modules/*/lesson.md finds no premium or coupon liability (far-revenue-measurement mentions coupons only as consideration payable to a customer), no self-insurance and no ASC 410-30 discounting. far-payables covers only the warranty roll-forward.
source: Review brief §3 lesson–item alignment; ASC 410-30-35-12; ASC 450-20-25-8, 450-20-55; ASC 210-20-45-1
fix: Add a short "Measurement and presentation details" section: (1) no accrual for general or unspecified business risks or self-insured future losses, since no event has occurred; (2) "probable" means likely to occur, a higher bar than more-likely-than-not; (3) environmental remediation liabilities are undiscounted unless the amount and timing are fixed or reliably determinable; (4) a probable insurance recovery is a separate asset, not netted; (5) premium/coupon liability = expected redemptions not yet made × cost, with a worked line. Add an inline check on one of these.

issue: Unasserted claims appear only in a key takeaway, never in the lesson body, and the takeaway ("Unasserted claims are disclosed only if assertion is probable and an unfavorable outcome is at least reasonably possible") gives only the disclosure test. It never says that when assertion is probable and an unfavorable outcome is probable and estimable, the claim is accrued. Learners can read it as "unasserted claims are only ever disclosed".
evidence: Body: no mention of unasserted claims. Items far-cont-05, far-cont-28, fc6 and u12 t7 test the rule. ASC 450-20-50-6 sets the disclosure test, and the ASC 450-20-25-2 accrual conditions apply to unasserted claims whose assertion is probable.
fix: Add a body paragraph or two-step mini-grid: "Unasserted claim → (1) Is assertion probable? No → nothing. Yes → (2) apply the normal grid: probable and estimable → accrue; reasonably possible → disclose." Reword the takeaway to match.

issue: Guarantee guidance predates CECL. The lesson says that for guarantees of others' debt "If a payment later becomes probable and estimable, apply ASC 450". Since ASU 2016-13 (effective for all entities for fiscal years beginning after 12/15/2022), the contingent aspect of a financial guarantee in the scope of ASC 326-20 (an off-balance-sheet credit exposure) is measured as expected credit losses from inception, with no "probable" threshold. That liability is recognized separately from, and in addition to, the ASC 460 stand-ready liability. far-cont-06's explanation describes only the ASC 460 piece. Its key is still the best option.
evidence: Search results (Deloitte Roadmap: Contingencies, ch. 5 Guarantees; CohnReznick CECL roadmap; PwC In depth) say that a guarantee of a borrower's repayment is an off-balance-sheet credit exposure under ASC 326-20, and that the CECL liability is recognized separately from amounts under Topic 460. ASC 450-20 still applies to guarantees outside the scope of ASC 326 (e.g., nonfinancial performance guarantees).
fix: Lesson: "The contingent part is accounted for separately: for financial guarantees (e.g., of a loan), an expected-credit-loss liability under ASC 326-20 from inception; for other guarantees, ASC 450 when a payment becomes probable and estimable." far-cont-06: add "(assume expected credit losses are immaterial)" to the stem, or note the separate CECL liability in the explanation.

issue: far-cont-18 uses the traditional premium-expense model (liability = cost of expected premiums not yet redeemed) but does not say how the coupons were distributed. If they came with product sales, ASC 606 treats the premium offer as a material right: a separate performance obligation measured at its allocated transaction price, not at the premium's cost. The platform's own far-revenue-measurement lesson treats coupons as consideration payable to customers, so learners meet two models with no bridge.
evidence: Keyed (40,000 − 10,000) × $2 = 60,000 is right under the cost-accrual model. Under ASC 606-10-55-41 to 55-45 (customer options), a coupon delivered with a purchase that gives a material right defers revenue at its relative standalone selling price, so the stem has no data for that model. A search found Deloitte Roadmap 11.8 (vouchers, discounts, coupons) and study texts that still teach the premium-liability model, so exam treatment is uncertain.
fix: State that the coupons were distributed in a promotional mailing with no purchase required, and call the amount the "estimated liability for premiums". Or reframe the item under ASC 606, and add a one-paragraph contrast in the lesson.

issue: Sequencing and routing. The lesson defers recognized vs. nonrecognized events to "Subsequent Events", the next module (far-subsequent-events). Both unit TBS give about half their cells to ASC 855 content: post-year-end fire, settlement as a recognized event, and the available-to-be-issued date in the u12 note. TBS results are attributed to moduleIds[0] = far-contingencies (src/db/actions.ts:113), so misses on the subsequent-events cells send the learner back to the contingencies lesson.
evidence: Lesson: "information after year-end (before issuance) can help estimate it (see Subsequent Events)." r3 rows dd and e, and u12 t1, t4, a1, s1, s2 and s3, need ASC 855. The available-to-be-issued date (s1) is taught only in far-subsequent-events. src/db/actions.ts: moduleId: tbs.moduleIds[0].
fix: Present these two TBS only after far-subsequent-events is complete (unit-end), or list far-subsequent-events first for the subsequent-event-heavy TBS. Better still, attribute TBS results per cell to the module each cell tests.

issue: IFRS comparisons are presented as exam-relevant. The worked example's insight calls the IFRS midpoint "a classic U.S. GAAP vs. IFRS comparison", and fc3 adds "(IFRS: midpoint.)". IFRS is believed not tested on FAR since the 2024 Blueprints.
evidence: review/reference/far-standards.md §1c, IFRS row: "Believed not tested since the 2024 Blueprints" (from-memory/unverified). The IAS 37.39 midpoint statement itself is accurate.
fix: Reword to "The midpoint is not the U.S. GAAP answer (it is the IFRS approach, which FAR no longer tests)", or drop the IFRS note from fc3.

issue: The citations don't cover every rule taught or tested. The firm-purchase-commitment loss is ASC 330-10-35-17 and -18 (the lesson cites only ASC 440-10), and the items also rely on ASC 410-30 (environmental), ASC 606-10-55-30 to 55-35 (service-type warranties) and ASC 855 (subsequent events).
evidence: Lesson citations: ASC 450-20, 450-30, 460-10, 440-10. chk2/fc7 test the purchase-commitment loss; far-cont-07 and -14 rely on ASC 410-30; far-cont-17 on ASC 606; far-cont-27 and both TBS on ASC 855.
fix: Add ASC 330-10-35-17/18, ASC 410-30 and ASC 855-10 to the citations, and cite 330-10-35-17 next to the firm-commitment bullet.

issue: The answer-key letters are skewed: c and d are keyed 21 of 31 times (c 11, d 10, a 5, b 5) across the practice and exam MCQs, which gives test-wise learners a guessing edge.
evidence: Count over items.json, practice and exam pools: {c: 11, d: 10, a: 5, b: 5}.
fix: Rebalance by reordering the choices in about 5 items (e.g., far-cont-10, -11, -23, -24, -28) so that a and b are keyed more often.

issue: The two practice TBS largely duplicate each other: a lawsuit with a range, assurance warranties on $2,000,000 of sales, an uninsured post-year-end warehouse fire, and a lawsuit settled after year-end. Both use the same accrue/disclose/neither dropdown. Neither has a research part (e.g., ASC 450-20-25-2) or a journal-entry part, so the second TBS adds little new practice.
evidence: r3: A (range, best estimate), C (2% × $2,000,000), D (settled Feb 10), E (fire Feb 20). u12: 1 (range, settled Feb 20), 2 (3% × $2,000,000), 4 (fire Jan 15).
fix: Turn r3 into a research part (cite ASC 450-20-25-2 or 450-20-30-1) plus a journal entry for the warranty and litigation accruals, or into a legal-letter documentation review (FAR-III.B.3).
